explain.say: Imagine you are clicking slowly up the first hill of a roller coaster. Your tummy flutters. Then, whoosh! Where does all that speed come from? It comes from energy moving between stores. Let us ride along and watch it move.

faq.q: Why does a roller coaster start with the biggest hill?
faq.a: The first hill gives the car all its energy. Later hills must be lower because some energy is lost to friction and air resistance.
asks: Why is the first hill the highest?

faq.q: Where does the energy go on the drop?
faq.a: Energy moves from the gravitational store into the kinetic store, so the car speeds up as it falls.
asks: What energy change happens when the coaster goes down?

faq.q: Why is each hill lower than the one before?
faq.a: Friction and air resistance transfer some energy to heat and sound all the time, so the car never has enough to climb as high again.
asks: Why can a roller coaster not go back up to the same height?

faq.q: Is energy lost on a roller coaster?
faq.a: Energy is never destroyed. It spreads out as heat and sound into the surroundings, where it is no longer useful.

faq.q: What does the motor on the lift hill do?
faq.a: It transfers energy from electricity to the car, filling its gravitational store as it is lifted higher.
asks: Why does a roller coaster need a chain lift?

facts: On the way down a hill, gravitational potential energy is transferred to kinetic energy.
Kingda Ka (USA) was 139 m tall and launched riders to about 206 km/h.
